title: One line at a time
summary: Keep a running note and update it each word, instead of rereading the whole page.

cards.text:
A long page makes a full attention table enormous.
A running note updates one word at a time.

Tips fit a note that changes when something arrives
and otherwise sits still.

choices: a running note, one word at a time
a full table of every word against every other
a frozen pond with no reader
question.why: The parent idea is a linear recurrent mixer, RWKV.
question.simpler: The claim is that this can be trained with spiking units, not that it matches the largest language models.

question.prompt: Each new word allocates a fresh row of scores against every earlier word.
question.why: The note updates. It does not rebuild the table.

recall.question: Why is a running note a better fit for tips than a full attention table?
recall.answer: It updates when an event arrives and can stay quiet otherwise.

deeper.note: Zhu, Zhao, Li, and Eshraghian. The preprint is the citation. It was later presented at ICLR 2025. Read how the spiking unit replaces the usual activation inside that recurrence.

paper.title: SpikeGPT: Generative Pre-trained Language Model with Spiking Neural Networks
paper.section: The recurrent mixer and what the spike replaces.

terms.plain: a running note, one token at a time
terms.definition: A sequence block whose state updates per token, instead of building a token-by-token attention matrix.
